Build a C-index heatmap from a train/test MAE pair

Source: R/visualizations.R
c_heatmap.Rd

Wrapper: harvests the metrics out of a train and test MAE object, tidies/classifies them, and returns the faceted heatmap as a ggplot object.

Usage

c_heatmap(
  mae_train,
  mae_test,
  name = "Dataset",
  aftcoop_rho = NULL,
  strat_order = STRAT_ORDER,
  metric_order = METRIC_ORDER,
  std_methods = STD_METHODS,
  modality_map = MODALITY_MAP,
  branch_map = BRANCH_MAP,
  metric_map = METRIC_MAP,
  single_omics = SINGLE_OMICS,
  fill_limits = NULL,
  text_threshold = NULL,
  palette = "YlGnBu"
)

Arguments

mae_train, mae_test

MAE objects exposing @metadata[["analysis"]] for the training and test splits.

name

Character scalar; the dataset label shown as the facet-column title. Defaults to "Dataset".

aftcoop_rho

Numeric scalar; the beta_rho value to select for AFTCoop results (e.g. 0.3, 0.5, 0.7). When NULL (default) all available beta_rho_* sub-keys are kept as separate rows. When supplied, only the sub-key whose suffix equals as.character(aftcoop_rho) is retained; rows from other rho values are silently dropped.

strat_order

Preferred top-to-bottom ordering of strategies. Defaults to Omics1, Omics2, Early, Late, Joint, Flexynesis. Missing entries are ignored; unlisted-but-present strategies are appended.

metric_order

Preferred left-to-right ordering of metrics. Defaults to H-train, H-test, Uno. Handled the same way as strat_order.

std_methods, modality_map, branch_map, metric_map, single_omics

Lookup tables used to classify and label paths. Override these if your path keys or desired labels differ.

fill_limits

Numeric length-2 colour-scale limits. NULL (default) derives a padded range from the data.

text_threshold

Value above which tile labels turn white for contrast. NULL (default) uses the midpoint of fill_limits.

palette

ColorBrewer sequential palette name for the fill scale. Defaults to "YlGnBu".

Value

A ggplot object. Print it to display, or pass it to ggsave() yourself if you want to export it.

Details

The result is flexible: only the strategies, methods and metrics actually present are drawn. strat_order and metric_order are treated as preferences — entries not present are skipped, and anything present but not listed is appended (with a message) rather than dropped. So a run with a single omics and a single method (e.g. only cox_lasso on Omics1) produces a one-row heatmap with no wasted space.
